newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil regional telcom monopolies seen for 3-5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil regional telcom monopolies seen for 3-5 yrs.

text.p: Brazil's planned private regional telecoms firms are likely to be granted monopolies for the first three to five years before the country is opened up to full competition, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said.
"In a first phase, there will be a monopolistic atmosphere," Motta told reporters.

He said that the four regional firms and long-distance unit Embratel created from the break-up of federal giant Telebras would face competition from three national operators after their monopoly status ends.
After the initial monopolies expire, Motta said he foresees allowing national operators to provide any telecommunications service anywhere in Brazil.
He did not give details on who those national operators are likely to be.
Motta made the statements during a news conference called to explain and answer questions on a proposed new General Telecommunications Law that was sent to Congress on Thursday.
The bill would create a law that establishes a regulatory watchdog, provides guidelines for the sector and creates the framwork for breaking up Telebras.
